avoid.reason: Very safe; car break-ins and theft at beaches/trailheads — leave nothing in cars

hood_desc: Waikiki is the iconic high-rise beach resort district packed with hotels, shopping and nightlife, best for first-time visitors and beach lovers who want to be in the middle of the action.
Ala Moana centers on a massive open-air mall and a calm beach park, suiting shoppers and travelers who want a central base near Waikiki without the resort crowds.
Kakaako is a revitalized urban district full of street murals, craft breweries, modern condos and hip cafes, ideal for younger travelers and creatives who like a walkable artsy scene.
Manoa is a lush green residential valley near the University of Hawaii with frequent rain and waterfall hikes, best for nature lovers wanting a quiet local neighborhood feel.
Chinatown is a historic downtown quarter with lively markets, art galleries, lei shops and buzzing restaurants, great for foodies and culture seekers though grittier after dark.

water.note: Tap water is treated and safe to drink.

transit.pay: The HOLO card is the main fare card (a $2 one-time fee, then loaded with value or a pass) and is sold at ABC Stores, Foodland, Longs Drugs, vending machines and the HOLO app; conventional contactless bank-card tap is not yet standard, so cash (exact fare) or a HOLO card is best. A single ride is $3.25 and a 24-hour day pass $7.50, valid on both TheBus and Skyline.
transit.hours: Most TheBus routes run from about 4:30am to around midnight (a few late-night routes), while Skyline rail runs daily 4am-10:30pm with no overnight service.
transit.note: TheBus and the expanding Skyline rail cover Honolulu well, but many attractions (North Shore, Hanauma Bay, hiking trails) are far from any route, so most visitors rent a car or use rideshare for full-island exploration.
